# Hanoi Motorbike Guide (en.rentbikehanoi.com)

> English-language guides on renting and riding a motorbike in Hanoi and Vietnam, published by Hanoi Motorbike Rental Nguyen Tu, a motorbike rental shop at 112 Nguyen Van Cu Street, Bo De, Long Bien, Hanoi, Vietnam (open 09:00-21:00 daily; phone, WhatsApp and Zalo +84 942 467 674). 981 verified guides across 14 topics, written for tourists, expats, teachers and students. Business facts (prices, deposit, hours, policies) are owner-approved; legal guides cite the primary Vietnamese sources (Law 36/2024/QH15, Decree 168/2024/ND-CP) and show their review date.

## Start here

- [Hanoi Motorbike Rental](https://en.rentbikehanoi.com/topics/rental/): how renting works, published prices, documents, deposits, delivery
- [Monthly Motorbike Rental](https://en.rentbikehanoi.com/topics/monthly-rental/): monthly rates and long-stay rental for expats, teachers and students
- [Vietnam Motorbike Laws and Licences](https://en.rentbikehanoi.com/topics/law-licences/): A1 and A licence classes, IDP rules for foreigners, fines
- [Customer FAQ](https://en.rentbikehanoi.com/faq/): 52 answers on prices, licences, deposits, 50cc and electric bikes, delivery and safety
- [Contact Nguyen Tu](https://en.rentbikehanoi.com/contact/): address, hours, phone, WhatsApp, Zalo, map
- [About](https://en.rentbikehanoi.com/about/): who publishes this site and how facts are verified

## Key facts (owner-approved)

- Published daily rates: Honda Wave, Yamaha Sirius, Honda Click, Yamaha Mio 150,000 VND; Honda Vision, Honda Air Blade, E-Bike 200,000 VND. Weekly and monthly rates are published for the Vision, Air Blade, Click and Mio; other models on request.
- Deposit typically 2,000,000-5,000,000 VND depending on the bike; the shop does not hold passports. Late return 20,000 VND per hour. Nguyen Tu does not provide rider insurance. Payment by cash, bank transfer or QR.
- Riding legally in Vietnam needs a Vietnamese licence or a home motorcycle licence with a 1968 Vienna Convention IDP; a new A1 covers up to 125 cc; mopeds of 50 cc or less and electric machines of 4 kW or less are licence-free from age 16.
